chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadhdha', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When it was the conquest of the day of Mecca, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stood among the people as a preacher, praised Allah and glorified Him, then he said: 'O People, let the one present convey to the one absent that verily Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has removed from you through Islam the haughtiness of the Age of Ignorance and the boasting about forefathers and clans. O People, verily you are from Adam and Adam was from clay. Behold, verily the best of you in the sight of Allah and the noblest of you before Him on this day are those who are most Godwary and most submissive to Him. Behold, being Arab is not by parentage but a speaking tongue. So whoever is reviled among you and knows that it will make him attain the pleasure of Allah, that is sufficient for him. Behold, verily all blood, or injustice, or malice that was in the Age of Ignorance will remain under my feet until the Day of Judgment.'

key_terms.نَخْوَةَ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ: Haughtiness/pride of the Age of Ignorance

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet declare about tribal arrogance and lineage during the Conquest of Mecca?
ai.summary: In this sermon delivered upon the Conquest of Mecca, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his progeny) formally abolished the pre-Islamic concept of 'nakhwa' (tribal haughtiness) and lineage-based superiority, establishing piety (taqwa) as the sole criterion for honor. He clarified that Arab identity is linguistic rather than genealogical and declared the nullification of all pre-Islamic blood feuds and grievances, a ruling that Shia scholars highlight as the foundation for social equality and the end of tribalism. This event marks a pivotal shift in Islamic social structure, reinforcing the principle that true nobility is derived from spiritual devotion rather than ancestral prestige.
